source.text: RF/EMI Interference Some factory environments may have equipment that gener- ates Radio Frequency (RF) or Electro-Magnetic Interference (EMI). These signals in close proximity to the Eastman cutting system can generate electrical noise and cause problems for the machine and computer (Eastman does offer a shielded mouse). It is recommended that any RF Welders or other equipment generating RF or EMI noise be a mini- mum of 75 feet (23 meter) from the Eastman cutting system.

Problems of this nature are typically difficult to resolve and must be approached in a systematic manner. To reduce the effects of electrical noise generated by RF, Eastman Ma- chine Company has the following recommendations:
Step 2) Enclose all AC power cables in rigid conduit and secure to the earth ground. Route the four power cables for the computer controls around the end of the conveyor instead of under the unit.
Step 3) Ground conduits to the table frames.

Step 4) Implementation of the foregoing should reduce the level of interference to a workable level. In the event that RF is still determined an issue, installation of RF filters and/or power line filters may be required.

source.text: tional pause Description of Problem: The machine stops in middle of cut and displays message “Machine Paused, Press Zero, Next or Abort” on Touch Screen. When pressing NEXT on the keypad, the machine will continue to cut where it left off. This is typically caused by an intermittent pause circuit, usually in thestop discs.

Troubleshooting: 1.Check stop disc activation. The stop discs should not activate by a slight touch or vibration. They should activate only when moved by minimum pressure. Remove gantry side cover. Check the pause plunger. Tighten the plunger to increase activation pressure and loosen to decrease activation pressure.

proposal: 1. FailureMode 'Intermittent pause circuit, usually in the stop discs' -> AFFECTS -> Component 'Pause plunger'. Meaning: The failure mode affects the specified component.

2. FailureMode 'Intermittent pause circuit, usually in the stop discs' -> RESOLVED_BY -> CorrectiveAction 'Loosen the pause plunger to decrease activation pressure' [repair]. Meaning: The failure mode may be resolved by the specified corrective action. Conditions: to decrease activation pressure.

source.text: Problem: The Cutting Tool or Pen does not move down Description of Problem: The tool or Pen does not move down when cutting a file or they are delayed coming down at the beginning of a cut. This can be caused by an electrical short, tool mapping in software or a problem with the power supply.
2.Verify the mapping of your tools and layers are mapped properly under each tool.
a)Look at the tool bar at the bottom of the Cut window to
quickly verify tool and layer mapping. If there is no Tool Bar as shown, then click on “View” then click on “Layers” and “Tools” in the main E-Suite menu.
b)If the layer is not mapped to a tool or the tool is not on the
tool holder then just click and drag the tool to the spindle or the layer to the tool before sending the file to the cutter.
3.With E-Suite closed, check tool holder to see if it moves freely and is not damaged or bent.
4.Make sure you have pressure at the tools. Try pulling tool the holder down by hand to see if it has pressure.

2. Symptom 'Cutting tool or pen does not move down, or is delayed coming down' -> MAY_INDICATE -> FailureMode 'Tool holder damaged or bent'. Meaning: The symptom may indicate the specified failure mode.

3. Symptom 'Cutting tool or pen does not move down, or is delayed coming down' -> MAY_INDICATE -> FailureMode 'Insufficient pressure at the tools'. Meaning: The symptom may indicate the specified failure mode.
